title: Analytic number theory, part III — smoothing, contour shifts and the classical Dirichlet series
summary: General analytic tools from a zero-free region to a prime error term (Fourier decay for bounded variation, principal-value inversion on vertical lines, rectangle residues, derivative Borel–Carathéodory, Landau's logarithmic-derivative lemma, Mellin smoothing, Ingham's transfer theorem, the classical L′/L bound for Hecke L-functions), the Dirichlet series of the classical arithmetic functions (complete multiplicativity, σ_ν, d_z, Ramanujan's identity, 2^ω, μ², λ, φ), the Hardy–Landau Tauberian theorem, Erdős problem 392 and the Goldbach-range propositions.

targets.name: BoundedVariationOn.tendsto_zero_of_integrable
targets.statement: An integrable function f : ℝ → E of bounded variation on ℝ tends to 0 at ±∞ and satisfies ‖f x‖ ≤ (eVariationOn f univ).toReal for every x.

tests.name: nonintegrable
tests.statement: f = 1_[0,∞) is of bounded variation but not integrable and does not tend to 0 at +∞.

targets.name: norm_fourier_le_eVariationOn_div
targets.statement: For f : ℝ → E integrable and of bounded variation on ℝ, of total variation V, and real ξ ≠ 0: ‖𝓕 f ξ‖ ≤ V/(2π|ξ|).

tests.name: sharp
tests.statement: f = 1_[0,1], ξ = 1/2: both sides equal 2/π; the constant 1/(4π) would fail.

tests.name: xi_zero
tests.statement: At ξ = 0 the right side is the junk V/0 = 0 while 𝓕(1_[0,1])(0) = 1, so ξ ≠ 0 is needed.

targets.name: fourier_le_of_deriv_boundedVariation
targets.statement: Let g : ℝ → E be integrable and of bounded variation with total variation V₁, and f(x) = f(0) + ∫_0^x g with f integrable. Then 𝓕 g ξ = 2πiξ 𝓕 f ξ for all ξ; ‖𝓕 f ξ‖ ≤ V₁/(2π|ξ|)² for ξ ≠ 0; and (1 + ξ²)‖𝓕 f ξ‖ ≤ ‖f‖₁ + V₁/(4π²) for all ξ.
hypotheses: ∀ x, f x = f 0 + ∫ t in 0..x, g t

tests.name: tent
tests.statement: f = max(0,1−|x|): V₁ = 4, 𝓕f(1/2) = 4/π² equals V₁/(2π·1/2)² = 4/π².

tests.name: zero_freq
tests.statement: At ξ = 0 the (1+ξ²) form reads ‖∫f‖ ≤ ‖f‖₁ + V₁/(4π²), true; the ξ⁻² form is not asserted there.

targets.name: one_add_sq_mul_norm_fourier_le_of_decay
targets.statement: If f : ℝ → ℂ is C² with |f t|, |f″ t| ≤ A/(1+t²) for all t, then f′ is integrable and (1+ξ²)‖𝓕 f ξ‖ ≤ (π + 1/(4π)) A for every ξ.

tests.name: lorentz
tests.statement: f = 1/(1+t²), A = 2: the left side at ξ = 0 is π ≤ 2(π + 1/(4π)).

targets.name: dirichletIntegral_bounds
targets.statement: With I(x) = ∫_0^x sin t/t dt: I is odd and continuous, |I(x)| ≤ I(π) for all real x, |π/2 − I(x)| ≤ 2/x for x > 0, and |∫_a^b sin(Tv)/v dv| ≤ 2I(π) for a ≤ b, T > 0.

tests.name: not_pi_half
tests.statement: I(π) ≈ 1.85194 > π/2, so |I| ≤ π/2 is false.

targets.name: tendsto_truncated_laplaceInv
targets.statement: Let g : ℝ → ℂ, c ∈ ℝ, u ↦ e^{−cu} g(u) integrable, G(c+iy) = ∫ g(u)e^{−(c+iy)u} du, and g of bounded variation on [u₀−δ, u₀+δ] for some δ > 0. Then (2π)⁻¹∫_{−T}^{T} G(c+iy) e^{(c+iy)u₀} dy → (g(u₀⁻) + g(u₀⁺))/2 as T → ∞.

tests.name: jump
tests.statement: g = 1_{u≥0}, c > 0, u₀ = 0: the limit is 1/2, not g(0) = 1.

targets.name: tendsto_truncated_mellinInv
targets.statement: Let f : ℝ → ℂ, σ ∈ ℝ, MellinConvergent f σ, x₀ > 0, and f of bounded variation on a neighbourhood of x₀. Then (2π)⁻¹∫_{−T}^{T} x₀^{−(σ+iy)} mellin f (σ+iy) dy → (f(x₀⁻) + f(x₀⁺))/2 as T → ∞.
hypotheses: f of bounded variation on Icc (x₀ − δ) (x₀ + δ), 0 < δ < x₀

tests.name: perron
tests.statement: f = 1_(0,1], x₀ = 1: the truncated integral is TauCeti.truncatedPerronKernel 1 σ T = π⁻¹ arctan(T/σ) → 1/2.

targets.name: norm_dirichletKernel_conv_sub_mean_le
targets.statement: There is an absolute C such that for h : ℝ → ℂ integrable and of bounded variation on ℝ with total variation V, and all u₀, δ > 0, T > 0: |∫ h(u₀−v) sin(Tv)/(πv) dv − (h(u₀⁻)+h(u₀⁺))/2| ≤ C (V⁺_δ + V⁻_δ + V/(Tδ)), V⁺_δ = variation on Ioc u₀ (u₀+δ), V⁻_δ on Ico (u₀−δ) u₀.

tests.name: tail_counterexample
tests.statement: h(u₀−v) = sin(T₀v)1_[δ,2δ](v): at T = T₀ the tail tends to (log 2)/(2π) ≈ 0.110 while ‖h‖₁/(T₀δ) → 0, so a bound by ‖h‖₁/(Tδ) is false and global bounded variation is needed.

tests.name: perron_rate
tests.statement: h = e^{−σu}1_{u≥0}, u₀ = 0: V = 2, V⁺_δ = 1 − e^{−σδ}, V⁻_δ = 0, true error π⁻¹ arctan(σ/T) ≤ C(σδ + 2/(Tδ)).

targets.name: truncatedPerron_instance
targets.statement: For f = 1_(0,1] and σ > 0 the truncated inverse Mellin integral at x₀ = 1/x is TauCeti.truncatedPerronKernel x σ T, and at x = 1 it equals π⁻¹ arctan(T/σ), tending to 1/2.

targets.name: rectangle_boundary_integral_eq_residues
targets.statement: For σ₁<σ₂, t₁<t₂, U open containing [σ₁,σ₂]×ℂ[t₁,t₂], P finite in the open rectangle, f differentiable on U∖P and meromorphic at each p ∈ P: ∫_{σ₁}^{σ₂} f(x+it₁)dx − ∫_{σ₁}^{σ₂} f(x+it₂)dx + i∫_{t₁}^{t₂} f(σ₂+iy)dy − i∫_{t₁}^{t₂} f(σ₁+iy)dy = 2πi Σ_{p∈P} TauCeti.Contour.residue f p.

tests.name: inv
tests.statement: f = 1/s on [−1,1]×[−1,1]: 2πi; the clockwise convention gives −2πi.

tests.name: outside
tests.statement: f = 1/(s−2) with P = ∅: 0; a sum over all poles of f would be wrong.

tests.name: double
tests.statement: f = 1/s²: residue 0 and the expression is 0.

targets.name: verticalIntegral_eq_U_contour_add_residues
targets.statement: Under 8.1a with t₁ = −T, t₂ = T and y ↦ f(σ₂+iy) integrable on ℝ: ∫_ℝ f(σ₂+iy)dy equals the tails over |y|>T on Re s = σ₂, plus ∫_{−T}^{T} f(σ₁+iy)dy, plus (∫_{σ₁}^{σ₂} f(x+iT)dx − ∫_{σ₁}^{σ₂} f(x−iT)dx)/i (top minus bottom, over i), plus 2π Σ_{p∈P} Res_p f.

tests.name: horizontal_sign
tests.statement: f = 1/s, σ₁ = −1, σ₂ = 1, T = 1 (finite-height identity): right π/2, left −π/2, bottom iπ/2, top −iπ/2, residue 1; π/2 = −π/2 + X + 2π forces X = −π = (top − bottom)/i; the clockwise model gives +π.

targets.name: caratheodory_coeff_le
targets.statement: If f is holomorphic on |z−z₀| < R with Re f ≤ M there and f(z) = Σ a_n (z−z₀)^n, then |a_n| Rⁿ ≤ 2(M − Re a₀) for n ≥ 1.
hypotheses: ∀ z ∈ ball z₀ R, (f z).re ≤ M

tests.name: extremal
tests.statement: f(z) = −2M(z−z₀)/(R−(z−z₀)): a_n = −2M/Rⁿ, so |a_n|Rⁿ = 2M = 2(M − Re a₀).

targets.name: norm_iteratedDeriv_le_borelCaratheodory
targets.statement: Under 8.2a, for k ≥ 1 and |z−z₀| ≤ r < R: ‖f^{(k)}(z)‖ ≤ 2·k!·R·(M − Re f(z₀))/(R−r)^{k+1}.

tests.name: equality
tests.statement: the extremal of 8.2a attains the bound at z = z₀ + r for every k.

tests.name: k_zero
tests.statement: k = 0: f ≡ i, M = 0 would give |f| ≤ 0.

tests.name: source
tests.statement: k = 1, f(z₀) = 0, r = R/2: 8M/R ≤ 128M/R, the source's bound.

targets.name: logDeriv_sub_sum_zeros_le
targets.statement: Fix 0 < r₁ < r₂ < R. There is C = C(r₁/R, r₂/R) such that if f is holomorphic near |z−z₀| ≤ R, f(z₀) ≠ 0, |f| ≤ e^M|f(z₀)| on that disc, then for |z−z₀| ≤ r₁ with f(z) ≠ 0: |f′(z)/f(z) − Σ_{|ρ−z₀|≤r₂, f(ρ)=0} m_ρ/(z−ρ)| ≤ C M/R.
hypotheses: ∀ z ∈ closedBall z₀ R, ‖f z‖ ≤ exp M * ‖f z₀‖

tests.name: linear
tests.statement: f = z − ρ with |ρ−z₀| ≤ r₂: both sides 0.

tests.name: needs_zero_sum
tests.statement: f = z − z₀ − ε: f′/f(z₀+2ε) = 1/ε while CM/R = C log((R+ε)/ε)/R.

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: M = 0 forces f constant: both sides 0.

targets.name: mellinConv
targets.statement: mellinConv f g x = ∫_{(0,∞)} f(y) g(x/y) dy/y for f g : ℝ → ℂ, x : ℝ.

api.name: mellinConv_comm
api.statement: For x > 0, mellinConv f g x = mellinConv g f x, with no integrability hypothesis.

api.name: mellin_mellinConv
api.statement: If (x,y) ↦ f(y)g(x/y)x^{s−1}/y is integrable on (0,∞)², mellin (mellinConv f g) s = mellin f s * mellin g s.

api.name: mellinConv_add
api.statement: Additivity in each argument where the integrals converge.

api.name: mellinConv_support
api.statement: If f vanishes off [a,b], g off [c,d], 0 < a, c, then mellinConv f g vanishes on (0,∞) off [ac, bd].

tests.name: indicators
tests.statement: mellinConv 1_(0,1] 1_(0,1] x = log(1/x) on (0,1], 0 on (1,∞); its transform is 1/s²; the additive convolution is the tent on (0,2).

tests.name: at_zero
tests.statement: f = 1_[0,1], g = 1_[1,2]: mellinConv g f 0 = log 2 but mellinConv f g 0 = 0, so commutativity needs x > 0.

tests.name: support
tests.statement: mellinConv 1_[1,2] 1_[1,2] has support [1,4] with value log 2 at 2, not the additive support [2,4].

targets.name: mellin_bump_bounds
targets.statement: Let ν : ℝ → ℂ be C^k, k ≥ 1, supported in [a,b], 0 < a ≤ b. Then mellin ν is entire, |mellin ν s| ≤ C(1+|s|)^{−k} on each strip σ₁ ≤ Re s ≤ σ₂, and mellin ν 0 = ∫ ν(x)/x dx.

tests.name: support_zero
tests.statement: ν = max(0,1−x)²: mellin ν s = 2/(s(s+1)(s+2)), not entire.

tests.name: sign
tests.statement: mellin ν 1 = −mellin ν′ 2 = 1/30 for the bump above.

targets.name: deltaSpike
targets.statement: deltaSpike ν ε x = ε⁻¹ ν(x^{1/ε}) for x > 0 and 0 for x ≤ 0.

api.name: deltaSpike_support
api.statement: Under the bump hypotheses, support ⊆ [2^{−ε}, 2^ε] and deltaSpike ≥ 0.

api.name: deltaSpike_mass
api.statement: ∫_{(0,∞)} deltaSpike ν ε x / x dx = 1.

api.name: mellin_deltaSpike
api.statement: mellin (deltaSpike ν ε) s = mellin ν (ε s).

api.name: mellin_deltaSpike_one
api.statement: |mellin ν ε − 1| ≤ C ε for 0 < ε ≤ 1.

api.name: tendsto_mellinConv_deltaSpike
api.statement: For f locally integrable on (0,∞), continuous at x > 0: mellinConv (deltaSpike ν ε) f x → f x as ε → 0⁺, locally uniformly for continuous f.

tests.name: eps_one
tests.statement: ε = 1 gives ν on (0,∞); without ε⁻¹ the mass would be ε.

tests.name: negative
tests.statement: deltaSpike ν ε (−1) = 0, avoiding Mathlib's junk value of (−1)^{1/ε}.

targets.name: smoothCutoff
targets.statement: smoothCutoff ν ε x = mellinConv 1_(0,1] (deltaSpike ν ε) x for x > 0 and 0 for x ≤ 0; for x > 0 it equals ∫_x^∞ ν_ε(z) dz/z.

api.name: smoothCutoff_mem_Icc
api.statement: 0 ≤ smoothCutoff ν ε x ≤ 1.

api.name: smoothCutoff_eq_zero
api.statement: = 0 for x ≥ 2^ε.

api.name: mellin_smoothCutoff
api.statement: For Re s > 0, mellin (smoothCutoff ν ε) s = mellin ν (ε s)/s.

api.name: norm_mellin_smoothCutoff_le
api.statement: For ν C^k, k ≥ 1, 0 < σ₁ ≤ Re s ≤ σ₂, 0 < ε ≤ 1: ‖mellin (smoothCutoff ν ε) s‖ ≤ C_k/(|s|(1+ε|s|)^k).

api.name: mellin_smoothCutoff_one
api.statement: |mellin (smoothCutoff ν ε) 1 − 1| ≤ C ε.

tests.name: half
tests.statement: for ν(1/x) = ν(x), smoothCutoff ν ε 1 = 1/2.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: smoothCutoff ν ε 0 = 0, so the n = 0 term of a smoothed sum vanishes.

tests.name: limit
tests.statement: as ε → 0⁺, mellin ν(εs)/s → 1/s = mellin 1_(0,1] s; the normalization mellin ν(s/ε)/s would tend to 0.

tests.name: uniform
tests.statement: k = 1, s = 1+iT: the bound is ≍ 1/T for T ≤ 1/ε and ≍ 1/(εT²) beyond.

layers.title: From a zero-free region to an error term

targets.name: smoothedSum_eq_mellinInv
targets.statement: Let a : ℕ → ℂ with LSeriesSummable a σ' for all σ' > 1, ν a C^k bump (k ≥ 1) with the standing hypotheses, 0 < ε ≤ 1, X > 0, σ > 1. Then Σ_{n≥1} a n · smoothCutoff ν ε (n/X) = mellinInv σ (fun s ↦ LSeries a s · mellin (smoothCutoff ν ε) s) X⁻¹.
hypotheses: 0 ≤ ν, support ν ⊆ Icc (1/2) 2, ∫ ν x / x = 1

tests.name: delta
tests.statement: a = δ₁: both sides equal smoothCutoff ν ε (1/X).

targets.name: norm_sum_sub_smoothedSum_le
targets.statement: If moreover |a n| ≤ B log(n+1) for n ≥ 1, there is an absolute C with |Σ_{n≤X} a n − Σ_{n≥1} a n smoothCutoff ν ε (n/X)| ≤ C B (εX + 1) log X for X ≥ 2, 0 < ε ≤ 1.

tests.name: plus_one
tests.statement: a ≡ 1, X = 2, symmetric ν, ε ≤ log₂(3/2): the difference is 1/2 while CBεX log X = 2Cε → 0; the +1 term is needed.

targets.name: inghamExponent
targets.statement: inghamExponent η x = ⨅ t ≥ 3, (η t * log x + log t).

api.name: inghamExponent_attained
api.statement: For η continuous on [3,∞) with 0 < η ≤ 1/2, the infimum is attained.

api.name: inghamExponent_mono
api.statement: Nondecreasing in x ≥ 1; log 3 ≤ inghamExponent η x ≤ η 3 * log x + log 3.

api.name: inghamExponent_ge_of_polylog
api.statement: If η t ≥ a₀ (log t)^{−A}, then inghamExponent η x ≥ c₁ (log x)^{1/(1+A)} for x ≥ 3.

api.name: inghamExponent_mono_width
api.statement: η ≤ η' on [3,∞) gives inghamExponent η ≤ inghamExponent η'.

tests.name: classical
tests.statement: η = 1/log t, x = e^{100}: the infimum is 20 at log t = 10 (= 2√log x).

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: η ≡ η₀: inghamExponent = η₀ log x + log 3.

tests.name: wrong_eval
tests.statement: η(x) log x for η = c₀/log t is the constant c₀ and gives no decay; the infimum over t is needed.

targets.name: norm_sum_sub_mul_le_of_zeroFreeRegion
targets.statement: Let η be continuous and nonincreasing on [3,∞) with 0 < η ≤ 1/2 and η t ≥ a₀ (log t)^{−A}; a : ℕ → ℂ with |a n| ≤ B log(n+1); r ∈ ℂ; U open containing R_η = {s : 1 − η(|Im s|+3) ≤ Re s}; G holomorphic on U with LSeries a s = G s + r/(s−1) for Re s > 1 and |G s| ≤ C₀ log(|Im s|+3)^{B'} on R_η. Then ∃ c > 0, C', ∀ x ≥ 3, |Σ_{n≤x} a n − r x| ≤ C' x exp(−c · inghamExponent η x).
hypotheses: ∃ a₀ A > 0, ∀ t ≥ 3, a₀ * (log t)^(−A) ≤ η t
∀ s, 1 < s.re → LSeries a s = G s + r/(s−1)

tests.name: classical
tests.statement: η = c/log t with 10.3 at K = ℚ (AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.33a) gives ψ(x) = x + O(x exp(−c√log x)), ZerosOfLFunctions §8.5.

tests.name: medium
tests.statement: η = A₀/log⁹ t gives exp(−c(log x)^{1/10}), kontorovichtao-pntplus line 1684.

tests.name: mobius
tests.statement: a = μ, r = 0, G = 1/ζ: M(x) = O(x exp(−c√log x)).

tests.name: constant_width
tests.statement: η ≡ η₀: power saving x^{1−cη₀}.

tests.name: steep_width
tests.statement: η = 1/2 on [3,T₀], linear to 1/log²(T₀+3) on [T₀,T₀+3], 1/log² t beyond (a₀ = 1/2, A = 2), log x = 2 log T₀: choosing T by log T = η(T) log x gives T = T₀ and left-edge saving exp(−2 log T₀/log²(T₀+3)) → 1 although inghamExponent η x ≥ log T₀; the route chooses T by log T = η(T+3) log x and saves 1/T.

targets.name: logDeriv_heckeLFunctionC_le
targets.statement: For a number field K, a modulus 𝔪, a finite-order χ : RayClassCharacter 𝔪, L = TauCeti.LFunctions.heckeLFunctionC χ and δ_χ = [χ = 1]: there are c > 0, C, an open set containing R_c = {s : 1 − c/log(|Im s|+3) ≤ Re s} and G holomorphic on it with L s ≠ 0 on R_c ∖ {1}, −L′/L(s) = G(s) + δ_χ/(s−1) on R_c ∖ {1} and |G s| ≤ C log(|Im s|+3) on R_c.

tests.name: zeta
tests.statement: K = ℚ, χ = 1 is AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.33a: with c = β, R_c lies in the open half-plane right of Part I's curve (log(|t|+3) > log(|t|+2)), G = −ζ′/ζ − 1/(s−1) extended across 1, |G| ≤ C log(|t|+2) ≤ C log(|t|+3), δ_χ = 1; §0.33's strip bounds multiplied give only log³.

tests.name: residue_sign
tests.statement: −ζ′/ζ has residue +1 at 1, so δ_χ = 1, not the residue of ζ_K (the class number formula).

tests.name: imprimitive
tests.statement: trivial character mod 2: L = (1−2^{−s})ζ, zeros only on Re s = 0; G differs by (log 2)2^{−s}/(1−2^{−s}).

layers.title: Dirichlet series of the classical arithmetic functions

targets.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative
targets.statement: For R a monoid with zero and f : ArithmeticFunction R: f 1 = 1 ∧ ∀ m n, f (m * n) = f m * f n.

api.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative.isMultiplicative
api.statement: It implies ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.

api.name: isCompletelyMultiplicative_iff_exists_monoidWithZeroHom
api.statement: f is completely multiplicative iff f is the coercion of a unique ℕ →*₀ R.

api.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative.pmul
api.statement: Closed under pointwise product for commutative R.

api.name: isCompletelyMultiplicative_liouville
api.statement: Holds for liouville, Dirichlet characters and n ↦ n^ν.

api.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative.pmul_mul
api.statement: f · (g ⋆ h) = (f · g) ⋆ (f · h) for commutative semirings.

api.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative.inv_eq
api.statement: The Dirichlet inverse of f is μ · f for commutative rings.

api.name: IsCompletelyMultiplicative.eulerProduct
api.statement: For summable ‖f‖ in a complete normed field, ∏_p (1 − f p)⁻¹ = Σ f n, from EulerProduct.eulerProduct_completely_multiplicative_tprod.

tests.name: moebius
tests.statement: μ(4) = 0 ≠ μ(2)² = 1: multiplicative but not completely multiplicative.

tests.name: zero_fun
tests.statement: without f 1 = 1 the zero function qualifies but is no ℕ →*₀ R for nontrivial R.

tests.name: infinitely_many_zero_primes
tests.statement: the indicator of integers with all prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4 is completely multiplicative and vanishes at 2 and every prime ≡ 3 mod 4; a finite-bad-set carrier (ArithmeticDirichletSeries §0.2) would exclude it.

targets.name: sigmaC
targets.statement: sigmaC ν : ArithmeticFunction ℂ, sigmaC ν n = Σ_{d ∣ n} (d : ℂ)^ν.

api.name: sigmaC_natCast
api.statement: sigmaC (k : ℂ) n = (ArithmeticFunction.sigma k n : ℂ) for k : ℕ.

api.name: sigmaC_eq_zeta_mul_pow
api.statement: sigmaC ν = ζ ⋆ (n ↦ n^ν).

api.name: isMultiplicative_sigmaC
api.statement: sigmaC ν is multiplicative with sigmaC ν (p^a) = Σ_{j≤a} p^{jν}.

api.name: sigmaC_reflect
api.statement: sigmaC ν n = n^ν · sigmaC (−ν) n for n ≥ 1.

api.name: LSeries_sigmaC
api.statement: LSeries (sigmaC ν) s = ζ(s) ζ(s−ν) for Re s > max(1, 1 + Re ν).

api.name: abscissaOfAbsConv_sigmaC
api.statement: abscissaOfAbsConv (sigmaC ν) = max(1, 1 + Re ν).

tests.name: sigma_one
tests.statement: sigmaC 1 6 = 12 = σ₁(6); sigmaC (−1) 6 = 2.

tests.name: abscissa
tests.statement: ν = −2: abscissa 1, not 1 + Re ν = −1, since σ_{−2}(p) ≥ 1.

targets.name: generalizedDivisor
targets.statement: generalizedDivisor z : ArithmeticFunction ℂ is the multiplicative function with value Ring.multichoose z a at p^a: generalizedDivisor z n = ∏_{p^a ∥ n} Ring.multichoose z a for n ≥ 1, 0 at 0.

api.name: isMultiplicative_generalizedDivisor
api.statement: generalizedDivisor z is multiplicative.

api.name: generalizedDivisor_natCast
api.statement: generalizedDivisor (k : ℂ) = ↑(ζ ^ k) for k : ℕ; z = 0, 1, −1 give 1, ζ, μ.

api.name: generalizedDivisor_add
api.statement: generalizedDivisor z ⋆ generalizedDivisor w = generalizedDivisor (z + w).

api.name: norm_generalizedDivisor_le
api.statement: ‖generalizedDivisor z n‖ ≤ generalizedDivisor ‖z‖ n ≤ (ζ ^ ⌈‖z‖⌉) n.

api.name: LSeries_generalizedDivisor
api.statement: For Re s > 1, LSeries (generalizedDivisor z) s = exp(z · LSeries (Λ/log) s).

api.name: abscissaOfAbsConv_generalizedDivisor
api.statement: = 1 for z ≠ 0 and ⊥ for z = 0.

tests.name: half
tests.statement: generalizedDivisor (1/2) (p²) = 3/8 and d_{1/2} ⋆ d_{1/2} at p² is 1.

tests.name: ordered
tests.statement: generalizedDivisor 3 4 = 6, the ordered count (unordered would give 2), as in AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §3.3.

tests.name: branch
tests.statement: riemannZeta s ^ (1/2 : ℂ) differs from LSeries d_{1/2} s by a sign where Im log ζ ∉ (−π, π].

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: z = 0: the series is 1 and the abscissa is ⊥.

targets.name: LSeries_sigmaC_mul_sigmaC
targets.statement: For α, β ∈ ℂ and Re s > max(1, 1+Re α, 1+Re β, 1+Re(α+β)): Σ σ_α(n)σ_β(n) n^{−s} converges absolutely and equals ζ(s)ζ(s−α)ζ(s−β)ζ(s−α−β)/ζ(2s−α−β); corollary Σ τ(n²) n^{−s} = ζ³/ζ(2s) for Re s > 1. The α = β = 0 case Σ τ(n)² n^{−s} = ζ⁴/ζ(2s) is AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §3.24a.

tests.name: tau_sq

targets.name: factorialFactorCount

targets.name: EvenGoldbachUpTo
targets.statement: EvenGoldbachUpTo H : Prop := ∀ n : ℕ, Even n → 4 ≤ n → (n : ℝ) ≤ H → ∃ p q, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n = p + q.

api.name: EvenGoldbachUpTo.mono
api.statement: H ≤ H' and EvenGoldbachUpTo H' give EvenGoldbachUpTo H.

api.name: EvenGoldbachUpTo.decidable
api.statement: decidable for each fixed H by search over n ≤ ⌊H⌋.

api.name: oddGoldbachUpTo_add_three
api.statement: EvenGoldbachUpTo H → OddGoldbachUpTo (H + 3).

tests.name: thirty
tests.statement: EvenGoldbachUpTo 30 (e.g. 30 = 7 + 23).

tests.name: vacuous
tests.statement: EvenGoldbachUpTo 3 holds vacuously.

tests.name: two
tests.statement: starting at n = 2 would be false: 2 is not a sum of two primes.

targets.name: OddGoldbachUpTo
targets.statement: OddGoldbachUpTo H : Prop := ∀ n : ℕ, Odd n → 7 ≤ n → (n : ℝ) ≤ H → ∃ p q r, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ r.Prime ∧ n = p + q + r.

api.name: OddGoldbachUpTo.mono
api.statement: H ≤ H' and OddGoldbachUpTo H' give OddGoldbachUpTo H.

api.name: OddGoldbachUpTo.decidable
api.statement: decidable for each fixed H.

api.name: oddGoldbachUpTo_of_primeGaps
api.statement: EvenGoldbachUpTo H, OddGoldbachUpTo (x₀+4), Δ > 1, x₀(1−1/Δ) ≥ 2 and a prime in every (x(1−1/Δ), x] with x ≥ x₀ give OddGoldbachUpTo ((H−4)Δ + 4).

tests.name: thirtythree
tests.statement: OddGoldbachUpTo 33 (e.g. 33 = 3 + 7 + 23).

tests.name: vacuous
tests.statement: OddGoldbachUpTo 6 holds vacuously.

tests.name: five
tests.statement: starting at 5 would be false: 5 is not a sum of three primes.

targets.name: oddGoldbachUpTo_of_primeGaps
targets.statement: If Δ > 1, x₀(1 − 1/Δ) ≥ 2, every interval (x(1−1/Δ), x] with x ≥ x₀ contains a prime, EvenGoldbachUpTo H and OddGoldbachUpTo (x₀ + 4), then OddGoldbachUpTo ((H − 4)Δ + 4).
hypotheses: ∀ x ≥ x₀, ∃ p prime, x(1−1/Δ) < p ≤ x
